title: Workload-matrix runner for hardware tuning profiles (H100/B200/L40S) + standardized summary artifact
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Motivation: The hardware tuning profiles pack needs a repeatable, SKU-aware benchmark runner that can (a) enumerate the agreed workload matrix, (b) run on the benchmark fleet (H100, L40S; B200 when available), and (c) emit a standardized artifact that downstream consumers (perf-canary gates, dashboards, and human review) can rely on. Today we have ad-hoc scripts and inconsistent output formats, which makes regression triage slow and makes it easy to compare apples-to-oranges across GPU pools.

What this PR does: Adds a new "matrix runner" to benchmark-lab that reads a pinned workload-matrix YAML, expands it into a set of concrete run specs (model family, seq-len bucket, concurrency, streaming mode), executes them across requested GPU SKUs/pools, and writes a single summary artifact (JSON + CSV) with a stable schema. The runner also captures environment metadata (runtime build SHA, CUDA/driver, GPU SKU normalization, profile pack version/selected profile, and runner version) to reduce ambiguity during incident response.

Key behaviors / design notes: (1) Matrix expansion is deterministic: order is stable and each run has a stable run_id derived from a normalized spec + seed. (2) The summary schema is additive and versioned (summary_schema_version="1.0") to avoid breaking perf-canary parsing. (3) Supports partial matrices (e.g., skip B200 if no pool matches) with explicit "skipped" results and skip reasons. (4) Emits per-run raw logs + a compact per-run JSON, then composes a top-level summary for dashboards and gate checks. (5) Adds basic guardrails around long-context on L40S (optional max_context_tokens cap and explicit "oom" classification) so the runner fails usefully instead of silently dropping runs.

CLI: `benchlab matrix run --matrix configs/workloads/hardware_profiles_v1.yaml --skus h100,l40s,b200 --pool bench-us-east --out artifacts/matrix/$RUN_ID --runtime-build runtime://redwood@<sha> --profile-pack <path|url> --retries 1`.

Artifact outputs: artifacts/<run_id>/summary.json (stable schema for gates), artifacts/<run_id>/summary.csv (quick spreadsheet comparisons), artifacts/<run_id>/runs/<case_id>.json (per-case metrics), artifacts/<run_id>/env.json (driver/CUDA/GPU normalization), plus raw stdout/stderr logs.

Non-goals: This does not change the workload matrix definitions themselves (those are owned in Confluence + runtime repo). This does not introduce new microbenchmarks; it only standardizes the orchestration and output.

Follow-ups: Once this lands, perf-canary will consume summary.json directly (ENG-4828). We also plan to add a small "diff" utility (compare two summary artifacts) and a dashboard ingest step for long-term trendlines.
commits: benchlab/matrix: add workload matrix parser + deterministic expansion (seeded run ids)
benchlab/runner: implement sku-aware executor + pool selection + skip reporting
benchlab/artifacts: write standardized summary.json + summary.csv (schema v1.0)
benchlab/metrics: add classification for oom/timeout/retry + stable error_reason fields
ci: add matrix runner smoke test + golden artifact snapshot
docs: add usage examples + troubleshooting notes (runner output + common failure modes)
changed_files: benchlab/artifacts/csv.py (CSV export with stable column order)
tests/test_smoke_matrix_local.py (small local-only smoke run with mocks)
docs/matrix_runner.md (how to run + how to read artifacts)
test_plan: 1) Unit: `pytest -q tests/test_matrix_expand_golden.py tests/test_summary_schema.py` 2) Local smoke (mock executor): `pytest -q tests/test_smoke_matrix_local.py` 3) Staging bench run (H100 only): `benchlab matrix run --matrix configs/workloads/hardware_profiles_v1.yaml --skus h100 --pool bench-us-east --out /tmp/matrix-artifacts --dry-run=false` 4) Validate artifact: `jq '.summary_schema_version, .cases | length' artifacts/.../summary.json` and open summary.csv to confirm stable column ordering.
conversation:
Claire Dubois (review): The schema v1.0 looks good, but we need to be explicit about units. Can you annotate tokens/sec (prefill vs decode) and ensure p50/p95 are in milliseconds? Also please include the workload "streaming" flag in the per-case record and the top-level aggregation.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Good call. I updated summary_v1 schema + docs: latency fields are *_ms, throughput is tokens_per_s_{prefill,decode,total}, and added streaming=true/false to case records + aggregation keys. Pushed commit `benchlab/artifacts: clarify units + streaming flag`.

Sofia Ivanova (review): For scheduler tuning we’ll want to correlate regressions with concurrency. Right now concurrency is in the spec but not in the CSV export. Please add it, and ensure the CSV columns are stable (same order) so we can diff two runs.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added concurrency to CSV + locked column order in csv.py. Also added a small golden CSV header test to prevent reorder churn.

Kira Volkov (review): Perf-canary needs deterministic run ids. Your run_id includes a timestamp right now, which will prevent caching/diffing. Can we split "run_group_id" (timestamped) from "case_id" (deterministic) and make sure case_id is stable across reruns?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated. case_id is sha256(normalized_case_spec + seed) and stable. run_group_id remains timestamped for artifact directory naming. summary.json includes both plus a stable "matrix_version" string from the YAML.

Aisha Bello (review): Can you add a minimal "gate-friendly" summary section at the top-level with precomputed aggregates per SKU (p50/p95, success rate, mean tokens/sec) so the canary job doesn’t need to implement its own aggregation? It’s okay if we still keep per-case rows.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added top-level `aggregates_by_sku` with explicit formulas and included both overall + by seq_len_bucket. Documented in docs/matrix_runner.md under "Using in perf-canary".

Isabella Rossi (review): Minor: GPU SKU normalization should handle the string variants we’ve been seeing (e.g., "NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3" vs "H100-SXM5-80GB"). Can we add a mapping table with tests?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `benchlab/env/gpu_normalize.py` with a small mapping table + unit tests. It’s not exhaustive but covers our current fleet strings; unknown strings pass through but are tagged `gpu_sku_normalized="unknown"` and include raw value for debugging.

CI bot: L40S runner smoke test failed (timeout) on `tests/test_smoke_matrix_local.py`.

Rina Kobayashi (author): This test is mock-only; timeout came from a real executor import path. Fixed by defaulting the smoke test to the mock executor and marking the real executor path as integration-only. Re-ran CI.

Claire Dubois (approval): Approved. This is the missing piece for reproducibility. Please make sure we pin `configs/workloads/hardware_profiles_v1.yaml` updates behind a PR review from Perf.

Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved.

Kira Volkov (approval): Approved.

Aisha Bello (approval): Approved, thanks for adding aggregates_by_sku.
release_notes: Adds `benchlab matrix run` workload-matrix runner and standardized benchmark summary artifacts (summary.json/csv) for hardware tuning profiles validation. Intended for internal benchmarking + perf-canary consumption; no production impact.
